Axiom:
Bootstrap Requirements with Owner=`this-scope-task` become the smallest coherent infrastructure workstream needed by the approved specification. Prefer one ticket; split only for a real independent outcome or the general `AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES` conditions. Do not manufacture one ticket per runtime, package manager, dependency, compiler, quality tool, or application platform.
Ownership remains structural: infrastructure rows use `infrastructure-flat`; product/library bootstrap rows use `scope-bootstrap`; module work uses `module`. `external-prereq-scope` becomes a cross-scope dependency and `operator-action` becomes an explicit blocking prerequisite in the index.
Express the implementation plan with ordinary ticket fields only: ordered phases, `Deps`, `Rules`, `Spec Refs`, `Target Files`, `Readiness Gates`, `Inputs`, `Exit`, BDD, and Verification. The semantic DAG must put every prerequisite before its consumer. For example, a repository runtime/version contract (`.nvmrc` or equivalent) and the selected package-manager contract precede dependency installation; dependency materialization precedes scripts, configuration, tests, and commands that consume those dependencies. Shared manifest/lock writers are serialized by phase/ticket dependencies.
`sdd-check --task ... --authoring` and `sdd-check --all .` validate structure, references, IDs, and dependency shape. The independent actual-ticket review judges whether the declared order is semantically sufficient and whether each real Verification command proves its requirement. No synthetic provider/package field schema or feasibility pre-plan/tool mode is part of this flow.
If Bootstrap Requirements is absent, stop scaffold and return to the owning specification flow; scaffold must not invent infrastructure requirements.
